harmfulIngredients.name: palm oil
harmfulIngredients.reason: About 50% saturated fat — raises LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular risk. Production is also a leading driver of tropical deforestation.

harmfulIngredients.name: high fructose corn syrup
harmfulIngredients.reason: Concentrated free fructose is metabolised primarily by the liver and is linked to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, elevated triglycerides, and insulin resistance at typical Western intake levels.

harmfulIngredients.name: corn syrup
harmfulIngredients.reason: A glucose syrup with a high glycemic load. Drives rapid blood-sugar spikes and contributes to total added-sugar intake far above AHA daily limits.

harmfulIngredients.name: hydrogenated
harmfulIngredients.reason: Industrial trans fats. Raise LDL ('bad') cholesterol and lower HDL ('good') cholesterol — the only dietary fat with no safe intake level. Banned by the FDA in PHOs since 2018 but residuals remain.

harmfulIngredients.name: red 40
harmfulIngredients.reason: Petroleum-derived synthetic dye (Allura Red AC). Linked to hyperactivity and attentional issues in sensitive children. Subject of the FDA's 2025 phase-out commitment.

harmfulIngredients.name: yellow 5
harmfulIngredients.reason: Tartrazine — petroleum-derived synthetic dye linked to hypersensitivity reactions (urticaria, asthma) and behavioural effects in sensitive children.

harmfulIngredients.name: yellow 6
harmfulIngredients.reason: Sunset Yellow FCF — petroleum-derived synthetic dye; one of the 'Southampton six' linked to hypersensitivity reactions and behavioural effects (hyperactivity) in sensitive children.

harmfulIngredients.name: aspartame
harmfulIngredients.reason: Non-nutritive sweetener classified by the WHO/IARC in 2023 as 'possibly carcinogenic to humans' (Group 2B), based on limited evidence. The WHO's JECFA reviewed the same data and retained the acceptable daily intake of 40 mg/kg body weight, finding no sufficient reason to change it.

harmfulIngredients.name: sucralose
harmfulIngredients.reason: Heat-stable synthetic sweetener. Recent research on its metabolite sucralose-6-acetate raises genotoxicity concerns. May also disrupt gut microbiome composition.

harmfulIngredients.name: maltodextrin
harmfulIngredients.reason: Refers to standard (non-resistant) maltodextrin — a highly processed starch with a high glycemic index (~85–105) that can spike blood glucose. Distinct from resistant maltodextrin, a prebiotic soluble fibre, which this entry does not flag.

harmfulIngredients.name: sodium nitrite
harmfulIngredients.reason: Curing agent in processed meats. WHO/IARC classifies processed meats as Group 1 carcinogenic, in part driven by N-nitroso compounds formed from nitrites during cooking and digestion.

harmfulIngredients.name: sodium nitrate
harmfulIngredients.reason: Converted to sodium nitrite during digestion; same N-nitroso carcinogenicity pathway as nitrite. Found primarily in cured and processed meats.

harmfulIngredients.name: titanium dioxide
harmfulIngredients.reason: White pigment (E171) in candies, gum, and frosting. The European Food Safety Authority concluded in 2021 it can no longer be considered safe due to potential genotoxicity; banned as a food additive across the EU since 2022. Still permitted in the U.S.

harmfulIngredients.name: potassium bromate
harmfulIngredients.reason: Flour 'improver' used in commercial bread and rolls. Classified by IARC as 'possibly carcinogenic to humans' (Group 2B). Banned for food use in the EU, UK, Canada, Brazil, and several U.S. states; still federally permitted in the U.S.

harmfulIngredients.name: brominated vegetable oil
harmfulIngredients.reason: Emulsifier formerly used in citrus-flavoured sodas. The FDA revoked authorisation for its use in food in 2024 over concerns about bromine accumulation in body tissues, but stocks may persist on shelves.

harmfulIngredients.name: tbhq
harmfulIngredients.reason: Tert-butylhydroquinone — synthetic preservative used to extend shelf life of oils and processed snacks. JECFA's acceptable daily intake is 0.7 mg/kg; chronic exposure above this is associated with immunological concerns in animal studies.

harmfulIngredients.name: red 3
harmfulIngredients.reason: Erythrosine — synthetic dye the FDA formally revoked authorisation for in food and ingested drugs in January 2025 after evidence of carcinogenicity in animal studies (thyroid tumours in rats).

harmfulIngredients.name: propylparaben
harmfulIngredients.reason: Antimicrobial preservative removed from the EU permitted-additives list over endocrine-disruption (estrogenic) concerns; the EFSA was unable to set a safe acceptable daily intake.

harmfulIngredients.name: bha
harmfulIngredients.reason: Butylated hydroxyanisole — synthetic antioxidant preservative listed by the U.S. National Toxicology Program as 'reasonably anticipated to be a human carcinogen' based on rodent forestomach tumours.
